pages.title: What this unit is about
pages.body:
> 📝 **Strand 2 — Productivity Software**
Sub-strand 2: Introduction to Presentation

Movement, sound and video can make presentations unforgettable, when used wisely. In this unit you will add pictures, transitions, animations, audio, video, tables and charts to PowerPoint slides.

pages.title: Content standard and lessons
pages.body:
> 🎯 **Content standard**
- **B9.2.2.1** Demonstrate how to use Microsoft PowerPoint (Multimedia).

> 🧭 **What you will be able to do**
- **B9.2.2.1.1** Demonstrate how to add pictures and insert screenshots.
- **B9.2.2.1.2** Demonstrate how to animate slides in a presentation.
- **B9.2.2.1.3** Demonstrate how to add multimedia (audio, video), tables and charts.

> 🗺️ **Lessons in this unit**
- 5.1 Pictures and Screenshots in PowerPoint
- 5.2 Transitions and Animations
- 5.3 Audio, Video, Tables and Charts

**Core competencies developed:** Creativity and Innovation (CI5.4), Digital Literacy (DL5.1).

pages.title: Pictures and Screenshots in PowerPoint
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B9.2.2.1.1
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- explore clip art (icons and stock images) and screenshots on the Insert ribbon.
Use **Insert › Images › Pictures** (This Device, Stock Images, Online Pictures), **Insert › Icons** (modern clip art) and **Insert › Images › Screenshot / Screen Clipping**, exactly as in Word (see Unit 4 and Basic 8, Unit 5). The **Designer** pane (Design › Designer) suggests professional layouts when you add pictures.

pages.title: Transitions and Animations
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B9.2.2.1.2
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- demonstrate the use of transitions and animations;
- create a seven-slide presentation with animations and transitions.
[[fig:c9-f07|Figure 6: Transitions apply to slides; animations apply to objects]]
> 🪜 **Step by step — Adding a transition**
1. Select a slide in the thumbnail pane.
2. Click **Transitions** and choose an effect (e.g. **Fade**, **Push**, **Wipe**, **Morph**).
3. Use **Effect Options** to choose a direction; set **Duration** and **Sound** if needed.
4. Under **Advance Slide**, choose **On Mouse Click** and/or **After** a number of seconds.
5. Click **Apply To All** to use the same transition on every slide.
> 🪜 **Step by step — Adding animations**
1. Select an object (title, picture, bullet list, shape).
2. Click **Animations** and choose an effect: **Entrance** (green, e.g. Fly In, Appear), **Emphasis** (gold, e.g. Pulse, Spin), **Exit** (red, e.g. Fade Out) or **Motion Paths**.
3. Set **Effect Options** (e.g. bullets appear one by one), **Start** (On Click, With Previous, After Previous), **Duration** and **Delay**.
4. Open the **Animation Pane** to see the order, reorder effects or add more (**Add Animation**).
5. Use **Animation Painter** to copy an animation to another object; click **Preview** to test.

pages.title: Transitions and Animations (continued)
pages.body:
> 🛡️ **Safety first — Use animation wisely** Too many effects distract the audience. Choose one or two simple transitions and use animations to reveal points one at a time or to explain a process.
> 💻 **Practical session — Seven-slide animated presentation**
Create a seven-slide presentation on **“Cyber Safety for JHS Learners”** with a title slide, five content slides and a conclusion. Apply one transition to all slides, animate the bullet points to appear one at a time, and use a motion path to show a “hacker” icon moving towards a padlock.

pages.title: Audio, Video, Tables and Charts
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B9.2.2.1.3
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- use the Insert ribbon to add audio and video;
- use tables and charts in slides.
| **Media** | **How** | **Playback options** |
|---|---|---|
| Video | **Insert › Media › Video › This Device / Stock Videos / Online Videos** | **Playback** tab: Start (Automatically/On Click), Play Full Screen, Loop, **Trim Video**, Fade In/Out, Volume |
| Audio | **Insert › Media › Audio › Audio on My PC** or **Record Audio** (narration) | Play Across Slides, Loop until Stopped, Hide During Show, **Play in Background** |
| Screen recording | **Insert › Media › Screen Recording** | Records actions on your screen with sound |
> 🛡️ **Safety first — Embedded media and file size** Video makes files large. Use **File › Info › Compress Media** before sharing, and only use music or video you have permission to use (royalty-free, Creative Commons, or your own recordings).
**Tables:** Insert › Table, then style with **Table Design**. **Charts:** Insert › Chart, enter data in the Excel window, and format with **Chart Design**. You can animate a chart so that its series appear one by one (**Animations › Effect Options › By Series**).
> 💻 **Practical session**
Add to your cyber-safety presentation: a recorded voice narration on the title slide, a short video clip, a table of “Do’s and Don’ts”, and a pie chart showing the results of a class survey on social media use.

pages.title: Review: written and practical tasks
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Review exercises** — answer these in your exercise book or on the computer, then check with your teacher.
## Short answer questions
1. Distinguish between transitions and animations.
2. Name the four categories of animation effects.
3. Describe how to insert and trim a video.
4. State **three** rules for using animations effectively.
